A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HopWeaver research. All 27 pages of v1 and 31 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support reliable comparison despite retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original question-quality, QA, retrieval, reranker and polisher experiments, plus judge-reliability measurements in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds end-to-end RAG evaluation, larger-sample validation, human judgments and reasoning-path assessments.

M1.justification: The synthesis steps, MMR retrieval, simulated-feedback reranker, filtering and polishing procedures remain unchanged. The clarified fallback between direct recommendation and diversified search was already specified in v1's prompt appendix.

E1.justification: The English Wikipedia corpus, benchmark datasets and bridge/comparison coverage remain. Section 5.4 adds an end-to-end RAG scenario in which answers depend on retrieved context, extending the earlier separate retrieval and question-only/golden-document QA evaluations.

E2.justification: v2 Table 4 introduces a substantial new comparison involving Standard RAG, REPLUG, SuRe, FLARE and IRCoT. The comparator sets in the retained quality, retrieval and ablation experiments are unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include a separate 500-sample validation, 50 human-rated question pairs selected with LLM-score differences above 0.3, and a random 100-question reasoning-path audit. The RAG experiment introduces Llama3-8B-Instruct with a 2048-token input limit and top-five retrieval. Existing main evaluations are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds sample-size validation, human validation of the judge and manual reasoning-path assessment. It expands v1's brief GPT-4o error inspection into a quantified 49-case breakdown: 18 formatting differences, 29 reasoning errors and two insufficient-evidence cases. The original reranker and polisher ablations are retained and relocated.

E5.justification: Table 9 extends reliability reporting to human evaluation through majority/unanimous agreement and three-rater Fleiss' kappa. The existing judge-stability procedure—five independent runs at temperature zero, with SD, alpha and kappa—is unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the retained ablation results are unchanged. New results include RAG scores, dataset statistics, 500-sample quality scores and human audits. For example, Table 4 reports bridge F1 of 0.318 for Standard RAG versus 0.158 for IRCoT; Table 10 reports 92% correct reasoning paths. Table 9 reports 94% human-majority agreement, although Section 4.1 inconsistently states 92%.

T1.justification: The comparison-path definition is corrected: v1 Equation 6 begins with the self-loop (e1, r1, e1), whereas v2 Appendix A Equation 8 uses (e1, r1, e2) and consistent terminal indices. The remaining constraints, retrieval equation, loss and reliability formulas are retained.

C1.justification: The automatic synthesis and human-comparable quality claims remain. However, v2 adds a central contribution that HopWeaver discovers diverse reasoning patterns exposing limitations of advanced RAG systems, and broadens its stated value to challenging benchmarks and targeted training in the abstract, introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 interprets RAG performance gaps as dependence on benchmark-specific reasoning patterns. Its error analysis acknowledges formatting effects and occasional insufficient evidence, qualifying v1's attribution to model errors. Limitations now discuss backbone/corpus dependence, inherited bias and English-only testing; the two-hop focus remains documented in Appendix B.

D1.justification: Appendix H adds concrete RAG settings, including Llama3-8B-Instruct, e5-base-v2, input length, retrieval depth and FlashRAG prompts. Appendix B newly explains benchmark question-type selection. Existing synthesis hyperparameters, hardware, cost information and code-access instructions are largely retained.

R1.justification: A new three-part Related Works section substantially expands the previously scattered positioning around datasets, synthesis and evaluation. It distinguishes rule-based, neural, structured-resource and recent LLM approaches, adding works such as Du et al. (2017), Chen et al. (2024b) and HopRAG.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution list, conclusion and limitations are rewritten. Related work becomes Section 2, preliminaries move to Appendix A, and main-text ablations move to Appendix C. These changes substantially reorganize the narrative while retaining most method and prompt descriptions.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the tabular presentation with RAG, dataset-statistics, larger-sample, human-agreement and reasoning-path tables. Existing ablation tables move to the appendix, and table captions and floats are repositioned. The core diagrams, radar plot and reliability heatmaps are retained.

improvement.justification: The human judge-validation study and quantified reasoning-path audit address important gaps in v1's evidence for dataset quality. Larger-sample checks and end-to-end RAG tests further strengthen validation and practical relevance. These gains substantially improve the paper, although the 92%/94% agreement inconsistency and interpretation of RAG gaps as proof of reasoning-pattern diversity remain weaknesses.
